messages:
maya: heads up — seeing a burst of 429s from hosted us-west1 @ 08:10. customer traces + internal logs line up.
kevin: yep. GPU node pod queues spiked and admission-control started rejecting around 85% util.
sara: do we have what the 429 responses look like? headers?
maya: grabbed a few samples from the ingress: 
``
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 30
X-Redwood-Queue-Length: 118
X-Redwood-Capacity-Used: 0.87
X-Trace-Id: 01F...
```
kevin: X-Redwood-Queue-Length was added mainly for ops debugging — SDKs currently only act on Retry-After.
sara: right; SDK retry logic today: respect Retry-After, then exp backoff. it doesn't adapt client concurrency or use queue hints.
maya: customers on Dedicated saw earlier failures since pinned capacity means admission control trips sooner. we should give SDKs a better signal to avoid overwhelming fleets.
ops-oncall: idea: instead of raw queue length, send an estimated delay in ms (accounts for sequence length variance). that is much more actionable for client pacing.
kevin: +1. add X-Redwood-EstimateDelayMs and keep X-Redwood-Queue-Length for diagnostics. SDKs should treat EstimateDelayMs as primary.
sara: proposed client behavior sketch:
``
if (resp.headers['x-redwood-estimatedelayms']) {
  delay = parseInt(resp.headers['x-redwood-estimatedelayms'], 10)
  // opportunistically reduce concurrency, e.g. target = max(1, Math.floor(current * 0.7))
  await sleep(delay * (0.5 + Math.random()*0.5)) // randomized throttle before retry
} else if (resp.status === 429) {
  // fallback: use Retry-After + full-jitter exponential backoff
}
```
maya: also propose a soft/hard admission header so clients can change strategy: X-Redwood-Admission: standby|throttled|accepted. standby = try later, throttled = backoff+pacing.
ops-oncall: logging/privacy note: ensure headers don't leak customer PII when proxied through Private deployments. strip or redact if needed.
kevin: rollout plan: stage headers in staging tomorrow, enable SDK debug flag to log them, canary SDK changes for node/python next week. if stable 48h, flip defaults.
sara: add guidance doc: capped concurrent requests, exp backoff with full-jitter, and treat EstimateDelayMs as a hint (not a guarantee). cap sleep at 120000ms so clients don't wait indefinitely.
maya: i'll write a short RFC with header names, units (ms), semantics, and the SDK sketch. will link here.
infra-bot: created RED-3421 "client backpressure signals: headers + SDK guidance" and assigned to @maya.
kevin: one more: standardize units and a max cap on EstimateDelayMs (120000 ms) so SDKs don't block forever.
maya: noted. thanks all :thumbsup:
